ImageDescription.value: A high-protein, budget-friendly DIY alternative to the viral London strawberry cups. Fresh strawberries with chocolate protein pudding, showing that you can enjoy food trends without the "London price" and with better macros. To make this high-protein strawberry cup, you will need about 200 to 250 grams of fresh, ripe strawberries. For the chocolate sauce, use one 200-gram container of ready-made chocolate protein pudding, such as those from brands like Ehrmann, Go Active, or Valio. If you prefer a more intense chocolate flavor, you can stir in a teaspoon of dark cocoa powder. For extra flavor and texture, consider adding optional toppings like a teaspoon of peanut butter, almond flakes, chopped nuts, or crushed freeze-dried raspberries. To prepare the dessert, simply wash, dry, and hull the strawberries, cutting any large ones in half. Stir the pudding in its container until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency, then layer the fruit and the protein sauce in a cup and enjoy your healthy, budget-friendly treat. The homemade version costs approximately £2.40 (Poland), whereas a similar cup at popular spots in Warsaw or Gdańsk in 2026 can cost between £5.60 and £7.00 (28 to 35 PLN). By choosing the protein-rich option, you save more than half the money and provide your body with about 20g of protein instead of just simple sugars.

ImageDescription.value:
nothing that innovative tonight bento friends -- you've already seen me use a square box with flower garnishes once this week!

main compartment: leftovers from last night's dinner of homemade vietnamese spring rolls (mine are vegetarian -- bean sprouts, cilantro, basil, tofu, carrot, and glass noodles dressed with soy sauce, sesame oil and chili flakes), with yellow beet stars added for garnish, lined with a cabbage leaf and buttressed by pickled radishes, yellow and red tomatoes.

"3 o'clock" compartment: leftover fried rice with a yellow beet and purple potato flower garnish.

"6 o'clock" compartment: edamame in a silicone food cup, with yellow wax beans and red carrot sticks.

not pictured: homemade peanut butter/soy/sriracha dipping sauce for the spring rolls.
